notes: Single primary FX model entrypoint. Defaults are wired into main.py so calibration work has one canonical runtime target.
session_scope: Normal and stress sessions with event windows; no full Asia/London/New York intraday decomposition yet.
calibration_sources: CME Group, Strengthening FX Primary Liquidity on EBS (2024)
CME Group, Building a Healthy FX Marketplace (2023)
CME Group 2024 annual report, EBS Spot ADNV
CME Group, FX Traders: Lovers of the Light (2025)

calibration_notes.price_vol_scale: The volatility of the latent price per tick, as a multiple of the stress index. It was never calibrated and sat at a constructor default of 0.35, which put 35 basis points of price movement into every tick. Against a quoted spread of two basis points that is not a coherent market, and it was the reason the endogenous provider wound the pool down before the shock it exists to absorb. The value now maps one tick to one second of EUR/USD at six per cent a year, the realised figure for 2026, which sits inside the five to ten per cent range of a calm year. Stress raises the index fivefold and carries the price to thirty per cent.
calibration_notes.mm_alpha1: The coefficient multiplies price volatility per tick expressed in basis points, not the dimensionless stress index. The old value 320 belonged to the old units and cannot be interpreted in the current equation. The current value 0.5 leaves the EBS top-spread gate to the observable touch parameters and gives volatility a small, dimensionally explicit widening role; it is not presented as a separately identified structural estimate.
calibration_notes.amm_lp_rule: The liquidity rule is stated as a dimensionless change, dL/L = phi1 times the fee return over the period, less phi2 times the variance of the price over the period, less phi3 times the cost of the capital over the period. The earlier form added a fee in quote units to a stress index and divided by a liquidity measure whose units differ between the two pool types, so restating the same market with a price of a hundred and not one changed the constant product response by a factor of twenty six and reversed its sign. phi2 is the curvature of the rebalancing loss, one eighth of the variance for a constant product pool after Milionis, Moallemi, Roughgarden and Zhang, and larger on an amplified curve because it rebalances more for the same price move.
calibration_notes.amm_lp_participation: The primary runtime uses an endogenous provider population with a complete two-asset ledger and an outside option equal to funding_rate_scale, about 2.9 percent annualised at one-second ticks over 252 full trading days. No direct FX-AMM evidence identifies the EWMA speed, capital-adjustment speed, entry margin, entry patience or exit patience. The values alpha=0.02 and 290 observations are therefore a disclosed central design, not EBS calibration and not an estimate of AMM-LP behaviour; in particular the 290-second bank-order lifetime is not used as evidence about capital review. The adjustment cap 1-0.5^(1/290)=0.0023873 gives the central design a 290-second mechanical half-life under a continuously binding resize signal. These behavioural inputs are accepted only through a frozen joint sensitivity design and separate mechanism-identification controls. Warm-up blocks participation decisions until the return estimate has accumulated three EWMA horizons. The entry hurdle is measured relative to the provider's outside option and is separate from the numerical response scale used for position sizing. The zero-subsidy, zero-rebate primary run is a private-sustainability test: closure or no entry is an economic result, not a simulation failure. Funded arms debit an explicit sponsor account through a posted return and/or a loss rebate.
calibration_notes.routing_prior: amm_share_pct is a historical API name. Under the primary liquidity_aware rule it is a weak AMM prior, not a target executed share and not an EBS-calibrated moment. The prior can receive at most routing_prior_mix_cap=0.18 weight before cost, depth, alignment and venue-state scores. The cost-gap scale, prior cap, basis scale and depth normalizers are explicit design parameters and must be swept because they affect routed customer volume, AMM fee income and LP survival. Under fixed_share only, amm_share_pct again becomes a literal routing probability.
calibration_notes.funding_rate_scale: The cost of committed capital as a rate per tick, about three per cent a year across the two currencies of the pair at one second to the tick. The stress index funding_cost keeps its own role and scales this rate, but it is not a rate itself and could not be added to one.
calibration_notes.amm_lp_phi2_hfmm: Removed as a free parameter. The loss curvature of the amplified curve is not a choice, it follows from the curve. Walking the pool to a nearby price and comparing the result against holding the reserves gives one eighth plus a quarter of the amplification, exact to four decimal places from an amplification of one to forty, and the same measurement returns exactly one eighth on the constant product curve, which is the frictionless value in Milionis, Moallemi, Roughgarden and Zhang. At the calibrated amplification of eighteen the coefficient is 4.625. The earlier value of 2.25 was assumed and understated the loss by more than half.
calibration_notes.enable_cpmm: The constant product pool is no longer a co-resident venue of the market. Its curvature is wrong for a pair that trades in a narrow band, which is the reason the amplified curve exists, and in the calibrated configuration it carried a small share of the flow and a small share of the provider result. Holding two facilities at once also made the committed capital of the facility an awkward object to state, since the resource matched comparison needs one number for it. The pool is retained in two roles. It anchors the measurement of the rebalancing curvature, where reproducing the frictionless one eighth exactly is what makes the measured 1/8 + A/4 credible, and it is the unamplified arm of the resource matched comparison, run one pool at a time so that the two curves do not compete for the same flow. Set enable_cpmm to 1 to restore the earlier two pool market.
calibration_notes.spread_block_ebs: The quoted spread is anchored to the primary interdealer venue, which for EUR/USD is EBS. CME reports an average top-of-book spread of 0.89 pips for 2025 and 0.74 for 2024; the 2025 figure at a rate near 1.10 is 0.81 bps, and that is the gate. Until 15.08.2026 the realised spread was not a market outcome at all. The price grid was a constructor default of half a basis point, absent from this manifest, and the book sat on exactly one tick in about nine periods in ten across grids spanning a factor of twenty-two, so the spread was the grid plus a thin tail. The cause was not the grid alone: the dealer left a quote to age until it had drifted twenty basis points, in a market whose spread is under one, so the mid drifted onto an old order and the best price in the market was one the dealer would no longer have chosen. Its best quote stood on the minimum increment three periods in four. The grid is now a declared input at the EBS increment of a tenth of a pip, and a resting dealer quote is withdrawn once the price has come inside a fraction of the spread that dealer would quote now. The rule is one sided by design: a quote the price has moved away from is left to age, which is where a bank's liquidity belongs and why its orders live as long as the published median says they do, while a quote the price has moved onto is withdrawn. Tightening the drift tolerance instead fixed the spread and destroyed the order-lifetime gate, because it amended the deep ladder too. fast_lp_base_spread_bps and mm_stale_touch_ratio now set the touch; mm_alpha0_base does not, because the dealer already targets several basis points and the binding constraint was staleness and not level.
calibration_notes.flow_persistence_after_ebs_spread: The ordinary taker classes retain heterogeneous private sign persistence and also respond weakly to the last observed common CLOB imbalance. With common_flow_response=0.30, the eight-seed median lag-one signed-flow autocorrelation is about 0.072 and the median run length about 2.19. This low-confidence order-flow block is diagnostic and not a publication gate because the cited EBS study establishes serial dependence but does not identify these simulator transition probabilities.
calibration_notes.background_book_size: The anonymous scaffold has been reduced from one thousand orders to ten and is capped at two per cent of near-mid support. It exists only to keep the numerical domain defined outside agent quotes. Every anonymous fill now settles against an explicit background-liquidity account in base and quote, so the layer no longer creates or destroys either asset. Agent-owned orders are never moved by book rebuilding, and each provider owns cancellation and replenishment of its own quotes.
calibration_notes.mm_inventory_half_life: The dealer shifts its quoted mid against its own position, and the size of that shift sets how fast the position mean reverts. At the previous value of 0.3 basis points per unit the half life of the dealer's inventory was six seconds and the median absolute position was one unit against a soft limit of a hundred, so the dealer never carried risk. Bjonnes and Rime report median inventory half lives for foreign exchange dealers ranging from under one minute to fifteen, and Lyons is the original single dealer study of the same quantity, so the model was between ten and a hundred and fifty times too fast. At 0.01 the measured half life is sixty five seconds, which sits inside that range at its lower edge, and the median position is seven per cent of the limit with excursions to half of it. The half life does not lengthen further below this value because the balance sheet controls and the mean reversion of the flow itself also flatten the position, so sixty five seconds is where this lever saturates. The consequence that matters is that the dealer now carries a position into a shock and loses on it: the loss component of the withdrawal score in the crisis window rises four fold.
calibration_notes.mm_quote_life: Maximum resting life of a dealer quote, in seconds. It is not the same quantity as the published median order lifetime and must not be set equal to it. The ECB contact group figure of 290 seconds is an observed median on a venue where a bank's order ends either by being cancelled or by being taken, and until 16.08.2026 this model produced only the first of those: an anti-crossing rule clamped a quote that would have traded instead of letting it trade, so dealers never took each other and the observed median equalled the cap. With the crossing rule corrected they do, the median falls below the cap, and no setting of the stale-touch ratio recovers it: measured across its whole range on one hundred seeds the median stayed between 220 and 229 seconds against a floor of 230. The cap is therefore calibrated above the target. At 400 the observed median is 285 seconds against the published 290.
calibration_notes.mm_withdrawal_score: Dealer withdrawal is endogenous to information available to that dealer: inventory relative to its soft limit, rolling mark-to-market loss relative to initial capital, observed CLOB order-flow imbalance, current book liquidity, price volatility and funding. AMM support remains a quote-interaction diagnostic and is not an additive exit term: its earlier positive loading saturated in calm markets and faded under stress, so it acted as a calm-only intercept and not a dealer balance-sheet loss. The score contains no shock-window flag, liquidity-shock dummy or preset name. Full exit requires two consecutive above-threshold observations; the first makes the dealer defensive immediately. The dealer-crisis preset explicitly sets force_mm_pause=false. Heterogeneous thresholds 0.7, 1.0, 1.3, 1.6 and 1.9 generate staggered partial exit. Because no external study identifies a numerical dealer-exit share for this episode, the 0.30 share remains a zero-weight diagnostic; the publication gate is qualitative and multi-seed and not circularly fitted to that number.
calibration_notes.price_tick: The price grid the book quotes on, in price units. It was a default buried in the exchange constructor and absent from this manifest while being the single largest determinant of the realised quoted spread. It is set to the EBS increment for EUR/USD, a tenth of a pip, which at the model numeraire of one hundred is 0.000909 price units or 0.0909 bps.
calibration_notes.mm_stale_touch_ratio: Fraction of the spread the dealer would quote now, inside which a resting quote is withdrawn and not left to become the best price. Calibrated jointly with fast_lp_base_spread_bps against the EBS spread and order-lifetime statistics: the spread gate pushes it up and the dealer order-lifetime gate pushes it down, and at 0.06 both are met. The lifetime sits near the lower edge of its band, which is the binding side.
calibration_notes.fast_lp_vol_multiple: Loading on price volatility in the quote of the fast automated provider. It was a constructor default of 1.0, absent from this manifest, and it is the only channel through which the quoted spread of this model responds to volatility at all, because the dealer's own width formula returns about 0.11 bps against a grid of 0.0909 and is therefore pinned to the grid. That made the spread nearly a constant. CME report the EUR/USD top-of-book spread rising to 0.89 pip in 2025 from 0.74 in 2024, about 20 per cent, while the volatility of the pair rose 64 per cent, an elasticity near 0.32. At the previous values the model returned 0.11 with a bootstrap interval that excluded the published figure. The constant part of the quote carries no volatility response, so raising it buys level at the cost of elasticity while the volatility loading buys both; the two were swept jointly on sixteen seeds. At base 0.30 and multiple 2.0 the calm spread is 0.92 bps, inside the 0.81 +/- 0.30 band and closer to target than the 1.04 the previous values gave, and the elasticity is 0.285. Reading the coefficient economically, the provider charges twice the volatility realised over the life of its own quote, where 1.0 would be actuarially fair compensation for leaving it exposed.
calibration_notes.fast_lp_base_spread_bps: Constant part of the fast provider's quote, lowered from 0.80 to 0.30 on 16.08.2026 when the volatility loading was declared and calibrated. At 0.80 the constant was 78 per cent of the quote, which capped the elasticity of the spread to volatility near 0.22 for this provider and near 0.11 for the market. The pair is calibrated jointly and neither value should be moved alone.
calibration_notes.dealer_capacity_cascade: Until 16.08.2026 systemic liquidity was entirely exogenous. It responded to volatility, funding cost and an exogenous liquidity shock, but never to what the dealer sector had actually done, so a shock could empty the book without the emptiness making conditions any worse, and no dealer leaving ever pushed the next one closer to leaving. The model had no cascade in it. dealer_cascade_gain adds that channel and dealer_capacity_threshold sets where it starts. The form follows BIS Working Paper 1138, which finds that limited dealer intermediation capacity worsens illiquidity only at high levels of balance sheet utilisation: below the threshold nothing propagates, above it the marginal loss bites and bites convexly, which is why the term is squared. Capacity is read from the depth each dealer actually supplies relative to its own unimpaired quote, so a dealer quoting defensively at a fraction of its size counts as that fraction and one that has withdrawn counts as zero; headcount and depth are the same measurement here and are not added twice. Measured over eight seeds the impairment is 0.012 to 0.019 in calm, 0.91 with a peak of 1.00 in the dealer liquidity crisis window, 0.31 at peak in the flash crash and 0.13 in the funding shock. A threshold of 0.5 therefore never binds in calm, which leaves the calm gates untouched, and fires only in the scenario built around dealer balance sheet stress, which is the scenario the cited finding is about. The gain has no published magnitude at this frequency and is a disclosed design parameter reported with its sensitivity, not an estimate. A gain of zero reproduces the previous model exactly and the regression fingerprint confirms it.
calibration_notes.dealer_cascade_gain_choice: Set to 4.0, the smallest gain in the tested set at which the channel is measurable on the whole panel. Two earlier readings said it was inert and both were wrong for reasons worth recording. The first, on 40 seeds, gave +0.16 [+0.03, +0.33] on the peak spread and did not replicate. The second, on 120 seeds at gains up to 2.0, found nothing, and the fault was in the test and in the level: the term multiplies friction by 1 + g e^2 with e the excess of impaired capacity over the threshold normalised by the distance from the threshold to one, so at the median impairment of 0.39 the excess is 0.19 and the multiplier at a gain of 2.0 is 1.06. A six per cent change in friction is not detectable, and averaging over a panel where 8 per cent of seeds never cross the threshold at all dilutes it further. Measured on 200 paired seeds at a gain of 4.0 the effect is +0.17 [+0.01, +0.34] on the peak spread and +18.7 [+6.9, +31.5] on cumulative excess spread, both excluding zero, and it rises with impaired capacity as a threshold channel should: conditioning on the baseline arm reaching an impairment above 0.50 gives +0.46 [+0.05, +0.94] on the peak. Conditioning is on the baseline, so the treatment cannot select the subsample. No published study fixes the magnitude at this frequency, so the gain remains a design value carried with its sensitivity.
calibration_notes.mm_softlimit: Inventory beyond which a dealer stands down. It was a constructor default of 100, absent from this manifest, and it is what decides when a dealer leaves, because the withdrawal score in a calm market is almost entirely the inventory term: measured over twenty seeds its median is 0.135 and its maximum 0.670 against the most sensitive dealer's threshold of 0.70, while the loss term is zero to four decimal places. Dealers were therefore leaving calm markets on one path in eight through an ordinary inventory excursion, with no loss and no deterioration in the market, and the 300 seed panel put calm activation at 10.7 per cent against a ceiling of 5. The cause was not the inventory half life, which was lengthened from six seconds to sixty five to sit inside the range Bjonnes and Rime report and which repaired a dealer that carried no risk at all. It was that the limit stayed at the value calibrated when the median position was a single unit. Swept over 96 seeds in both scenarios: at 100 calm activation is 12.5 per cent, and at 150, 200 and 300 it is zero while crisis activation stays at 100 per cent, so raising the limit does not disable the mechanism. At 200 the median calm utilisation is 8.3 per cent with excursions to about a third of the limit, which is the profile the half life change was meant to give.
calibration_notes.dealer_cascade_form: The contagion channel is driven by increases in impaired dealer capacity above the threshold, not by its level, and the pressure it accumulates decays with a half life of 30 seconds. The level form was implemented first and is not usable. At full impairment it adds a constant g to friction, which holds systemic liquidity at 1/(1+g); for any gain above 1/0.55-1 = 0.818 that sits below the 0.55 a withdrawn dealer needs to re-enter, and because impaired capacity is itself the consequence of dealers being out, the state absorbs. Measured on the dealer crisis over 20 seeds, the sector stayed wholly withdrawn for 586 of 1000 periods at gain 2.0 against 244 with the channel off, with systemic liquidity pinned at 0.333 and under the re-entry gate on 89 to 100 per cent of the tail. Under the propagation form the tail returns to full liquidity and no dealer remains withdrawn. Bounding the magnitude of a feedback is not sufficient; its fixed point has to be checked against the conditions that reverse it.
calibration_notes.dealer_capacity_threshold: Share of dealer quoting capacity that must be impaired before the contagion channel acts. Set at 0.25, not at the 0.5 first chosen, because no admissible episode reaches 0.5 without the sector evacuating entirely. Measured across a severity gradient, impairment passes 0.5 in the median only where every dealer withdraws on most seeds, and widening the spread of withdrawal thresholds caps impairment at 0.34 instead. Enlarging the sector does not help either: at ten and twenty dealers spread over the same range of risk capacity the whole sector still withdraws together, because a common shock moves every dealer's score at once and the idiosyncratic part of a dealer's position is small beside the common part: measured over a thousand periods, dealer inventories correlate 0.65 on average across the sector and 0.95 at the closest pair. Heterogeneous exposure, not heterogeneous thresholds, is what would separate them, and that is a change to the dealer's inventory process and not a scenario setting. The threshold is therefore placed where the sector demonstrably goes, and 0.25 is reached on the identified episodes with full evacuation on a small minority of seeds. Nothing published fixes the number: BIS Working Paper 1138 establishes that impaired intermediation capacity worsens illiquidity only at high utilisation and gives the shape, not the point. Scaling total quoted depth and the soft limit together with the dealer count leaves the calm quoted spread at 0.800 for counts from five to twenty, so sector size can be revisited without disturbing the calm calibration.
calibration_notes.mm_client_flow: Private client flow each dealer internalises per period, with its own persistence and its own random stream. Most customer volume in spot FX is internalised bilaterally against a dealer's own client base and only the residual reaches the interdealer book, so a dealer's position comes mainly from a franchise that is its own. This model gave every dealer the same book to trade against, and the measured pairwise correlation of dealer inventories was 0.65 on average and 0.95 at the closest pair, which is what brings the sector to its withdrawal thresholds together. The trade settles at the reference price and moves cash and inventory together, so a franchise transfers a position without creating value. An intensity of zero reproduces the model without franchises, and the regression fingerprint confirms it: the private stream is created on first use and not in the constructor, because drawing its seed at construction would take a number from the global stream and shift every later draw. Set to 1.0. Measured over 16 seeds, the pairwise correlation of dealer inventories through the crisis falls from 0.961 without a franchise to 0.933 at 1.0, 0.842 at 2.0 and 0.566 at 4.0, while calm activation rises from zero to 0.06 at 2.0 and 0.38 at 4.0 and full evacuation appears at 2.0. At 1.0 the calm gates are untouched, the calm spread is 0.897, and no seed evacuates. It is the largest franchise that costs nothing measurable in calm.
calibration_notes.mm_core_threshold: Withdrawal threshold of the most robust dealer, placed above the ladder the others occupy. A linear ladder forces a choice the sector should not have to make. At a step of 0.30 every threshold is reachable by a common displacement and 7.5 per cent of crisis seeds lose the whole sector; at a step wide enough to prevent that, 0.45 and above, the middle of the ladder goes out of reach and the response collapses from five levels to two. Placing one dealer above the ladder removes the tail by construction and not by tuning, since the most a common shock can take is then four dealers of five. Measured over 120 seeds at 2.5, 3.5 and 5.0 the outcome is identical, because once the core is unreachable its exact level does not matter, and every other quantity is unchanged from the ladder without it: crisis activation 0.925, calm activation 0.008, calm spread 0.901. The peak withdrawn share then takes four levels across the panel, 0.2 on 64 seeds, 0.4 on 29, 0.6 on 6 and 0.8 on 12, where the linear ladder put 6 seeds at a full evacuation. The largest dealers went on quoting the major pairs through March 2020, so a sector in which every member can be driven out is the wrong object.
calibration_notes.arm_spread_bps: The flat price the obliged quoter is matched to, in bps of a round trip at the outcome size of two base units. It is the reserve priced pool own cost over the pre-shock periods, so the two arms differ in schedule and not in level. It was a literal in the comparison code and is declared here, because a pair prices its pool off its own quoting increment and its own volatility and the value therefore moves with the pair.
calibration_notes.crisis_scenario: The identified episode every crisis measurement is taken on. It was a literal in each measurement module and is named once here, so a branch calibrated to another pair cannot run this pair episode against its own targets without saying so.

manifest_notes.accepted_error_bands: This section mirrors observables that remain active in primary_model_targets.json, including diagnostics. recovery_half_life_ticks and cross_venue_basis_bps were removed when their targets were withdrawn. A test asserts that the two files cannot drift apart again.
